Direct facts
------------
- The selected/composed 0x34-byte matrix returned by halo4+0x100EBC is at
  RAX = R8 = 0x0000005B55340310 (RBP-0x90 for this caller frame).
- The full matrix matched byte-for-byte at the +0x101300 source (RBX), the
  completed type-1 temporary at [RBP-0x18..RBP+0x1B], the +0x106D28 queue
  record, and the later scheduler queue transfer.
- A hardware write observation first stopped after halo4+0x106DEB; the
  completed queue record was verified at +0x106E0A. This proves the normal
  engine copied the matrix; the debugger did not write it.
- WORD [R15+2] was 0 and R9B was 1. This is local/location-0, not a unique
  identity for particle A versus particle B.

Returned matrix decoded as 13 little-endian floats
--------------------------------------------------
  [0..3]   1, 0.5142785, 0.62159026, 0.5908832
  [4..7]   -0.82135653, 0.15874104, 0.54788196, 0.2467604
  [8..12]  -0.76708996, 0.59218425, 32.443993, -14.755244, 7.6890574

The selective type-1 consumer condition for this slot did not stop during a
short bounded continuation, so no final renderer consumer is claimed here.
